Comments: On 5/06/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection in response to a complaint (CTS-397312) at the Clara Jacques 2 well site in Wharton Township, Fayette County. A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) was entered into between the Department and Diversified on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site after in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216; after completion of plugging operations.The following was observed during the inspection:Significant tire rutting was observed in the access road. Due to the soft and damp soil conditions that appear to exist on site, the Department recommends that the operator consider additional E and S control measures as necessary, to prevent accelerated erosion and sedimentation from occurring on site. No excess loose sediment was observed in the two access road cross-culverts (photos 4, 5, 7, and 8). The Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan available is on site (photos 12 and 13). An RCE is installed where the access road meets the well site, in accordance with the E and S plan drawing (photo 10). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed on site in the locations shown on E and S plan drawing (photo 11). No well plugging equipment was observed on site during this inspection.Based on observations from this inspection, violations are being issued against the tire rutting in the access road.

Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Franklin Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/18/2023
Comments: On July 18, 2023, the Department performed an inspection of the EQT, Rohanna well site. The site is located in Franklin Twp., Greene County. The inspection was a routine inspection of the site. 3 wells the 1H, 2H, and 3H wells have been drilled to TD, completed and are equipped for production. The wellhead is tagged and in good condition with slight corrosion. No leaks where detected at the wellhead or surrounding area. A fourth well the 6H has not been completed. The Rohanna 6H was spud by Vantage on 12/15/2012. On 12/15/2012 Vantage drilled, set, and cemented 40' of 20" of conductor pipe. No additional drilling has occurred on the 6H well. The well permit expired on 12/2/2017. The permit has not been renewed in accordance with Department standards. EQT has not pursued drilling of the 6H with "due diligence". In addition, the 6H by definition is considered abandoned. A violation of the OGA3320(A) has been issued for failing to plug an abandoned well. A violation of the OGA33211(i) has been issued for failing to drill the well with due diligence.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/24/2025 to KRIEBEL NATURAL GAS CO LLC in Manor Borough, Westmoreland county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8226588
Permit API: 129-28077
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Manor Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/24/2025
Comments: On March 24, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release. Present during today's inspection was operator representative Ronald Seich.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. All other production equipment was observed removed and loaded/being loaded onto a trailer for disposal.It appeared excavation had been started in the area where the production equipment was removed. Excavated material/soil was observed loaded onto tarps. No excavation appeared to have been started on the ditch. Mr. Seich stated that they planned on having all excavation completed, including the ditch, by the end of the day. He also stated that Moody would be onsite tomorrow (3/25/2022) to perform a site assessment and collect samples to evaluate their remediation.A soil conductivity reading was taken in the area where the production tank was previously located with a reading of 0.34mS. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of 16.00mS, 9.16mS, 2.30mS, 0.87mS, 0.83mS, and 0.80mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. A conductivity reading was taken in this area of the ditch with a reading of 0.34mSA conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.73mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings obtained, it appears that the conductivity readings are comparable to the previous inspections in regards to distance and levels of elevated readings in the ditch. It appears that released fluids may have been contained to the portions of the ditch where standing fluid was observed, and it did not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.Bases on today's inspection, violations remain outstanding.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on the (6) wells on the Cappucci pad. The Cappucci 4H, N 2H, 102H, N 4H, 2H and HJMM WYO 1H wells. This is the 3rd round of SPBUTs since remedial Perf. and Squeeze work performed on the Cappucci 4H, N 2H and the 102H was completed on 6/14/22. SPBUTs were initiated on 2/27/23 @ ~ 10:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - The (20x13) annulus was shut in on 2/27/23 @ ~ 10:00 - 72 hrs - The (13x9) annulus was shut in on 2/28/23 @ ~ 10:00 - 48 hrs - The (9x5) annulus was shut in on 3/1/23 @ ~ 10:00 - 24 hrs - All (6) wells annuli were shut in at time of sampling. - Upon arrival I met with Creston Consultants rep. Jason Rajan and CALLC reps. Giovanni Dicupillo and Dustin Wiles. Starting at approx. 10:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the Cappucci Pad wells. - Cappucci 4H (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 35,000 ppm (3)% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:28 (13x9): 19 psi..; 63% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:33 (9x5): 150 psi.; 74% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:36 - Cappucci 102H (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 0 psi.; 80% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:05 (9x5): 58 psi.; 80% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:10 - Cappucci N 2H (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 320ppm and dropping to 0% CH4; No sample taken (13x9): 19.5 psi.; 74% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:18 (9x5): 14.7 psi.; 75% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:23 - Cappucci N 4H (20x13): open top, No bubbling (13x9): 0.0 psi.; 12% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:52 (9x5): 0.0 psi.; 82% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:55 - HJMM WYO 1H (20x13): open top, No bubbling (13x9): 0.0 psi.; 90% CH4; Sample collected @ 10:43 (9x5): 0.0 psi.; 17% CH4; Sample colected @ 10:47 - All (6) wells (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened and venting to production tank and the (20x13) and the 2H (20x9) were opened and venting to atmosphere via Sentry valves @ 12:15 - The Cappucci 2H well has been recently plugged back, above the Lower Marcellus. The Shallower formations of the Lockhaven and Braillier have been perforated in order to produce the shallower gas. Well is presently shut in and not producing. - Creston Consultants were requested by Operator to obtain gas samples from outside tubing, the (5 1/2"x 2 7/8") annulus and from inside tubing. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for the Cappucci 2H well. - Cappucci 2H (20x9): O psi.; 4,240 ppm and dropping to 0% CH4; NO sample taken (9x5): 0 psi.; 95% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:05 (5 1/2x2 7/8): 387 psi.; 82% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:10 (2 7/8 tubing): 94 psi.; 82% CH4; Sample collected @ 11:18 (This is a (2) string well)

Comments: Met with Diversified supervisor Mark McCracken on 9/6/24 at the brine spill that Diversified reported on 9/5/24 for well 033-23855. According to Mr. McCracken a small stone punctured the bottom of the brine tank causing the release. Upon arriving onsite I observed where the release happened. I observed an excavated area approximately 35' long by 15' wide. Most of the main release occurred directly underneath where the tank was sitting. The brine tank has been disconnected and emptied. I screened the excavated areas using a soil probe. A few spots still have some elevated readings 1.15 mS/cm and 2.25 mS/cm. Those areas have been marked by the operator. The operator plans to remove the rest of the impacted soils on Monday. Two tri-axle loads of soils have already been removed from the site. In addition, I screened outside the delineated area. No other elevated areas were observed. For now, the hole has been covered in plastic. The operator will be using Act 2 for site remediation. A crew later today will be coming to install E and S controls around the perimeter of the spill. Violations have been cited.

Comments: On July 26th, 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a release that occurred at the Porter Well Pad in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County. The Department was accompanied by Justin Creighan (Olypmus), Bradley Latimer (Olympus) and Shelby (Olympus). On July 26th, 2022, at 6:56AM, the Department was notified by Operator of a release that occurred at 5:00AM earlier that morning at the 12M GPU on the Porter Well Pad. It was reported that approximately over 5 gallons of Glycol was released onto the pad. No impacts to local waterways reported. July 26th, 2022, the Departed contacted Operator for further information regarding release that occurred. Per Operator, around 5:00AM this morning, burner on the 12M GPU did not shut off and caused glycol within containment to release out of filler tube onto the ground and secondary containment. It is estimated that 30-33 gallons was released total. A clam shell was present onsite and crews excavated impacted area and deposited material into drums onsite. SDS sheets for Glycol are onsite and will be made available. On July 26th, 2022, at 1:15PM, the Department conducted an onsite inspection of the Porter Well Pad. At time of inspection, Act 9 Sign was installed at access road entrance (photo 1). ERP and PPC plans were present on site in mailbox. SDS sheets for Glycol were located on site and made available. Impacted area adjacent to 12M GPU appears to be visually remediated. Drums of impacted material were observed onsite within secondary containment. Release quantity determination was explained by Mr. Latimer onsite. Holding capacity for Glycol is 200 gallons, tube height is 6ft, and missing quantity is 1 ft (33.3 gallons). Mr. Latimer confirmed that quantity released was total amount released (within containment and released onto well pad). He also clarified that the thermostat that controls the burner to the GPU malfunctioned by not turning off burner to the GPU and overheating, creating the release of Glycol. The Department requests that the Operator submit waste manifests once available. Violations are being cited as immediately corrected/abated.

Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/21/2026
Comments: On 4/21/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/alteration inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 52 degrees and clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the active north pad, I met with Seneca's Adam Pierce who described current operations as follows: Evolution Well Services has been on site since 2/13/2026, performing stimulation operations on eight recently drilled gas wells. The crew was currently alternating between the 70HU, 204HU, 203HU, and 72HU. The crew has completed conducting stimulation stages on the other four wells. Adam expects stimulation activities on the eight wells to be completed by 6/8/2026.In addition to 28 frac tanks that were stationed on the west side of the pad during previous operations, four freshwater frac tanks, four pump down frac tanks, two gas buster frac tanks and five working frac tanks have been staged on the pad. These tanks are staged in secondary containment.Five wells have been completed at the site and were staged for production. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs that are connected to the completed wells are stationed in secondary containment.Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. During the inspection, I screened liquid in a 3' x 1.5' x 5" deep puddle, above the center outfall on the north side of the pad, the result being 9.40 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-242 from the puddle.I screened liquid flowing into the southeast corner of the sediment basin from the rock lined outfall from the pad, the result being 10.30 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-243 from the flowing liquid.I screened liquid in the sediment pond next to the east overflow, the result being 3.04 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-244 from the pond.I screened liquid flowing north from the sediment basin, past the last compost filter sock and past the LOD, the result being 3.33 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-245 from the flowing liquid.The original south pad and access road for the Taft 851 1V well have been returned to original grade with vegetation becoming effective. Separate construction projects are underway, installing water and gas pipelines on the south side of the pad.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1545 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/19/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/19/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 979236
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/19/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator about a release of an estimated 42 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and freshwater to the surface of pad B. The frac is on-going on Pad B. The site was snow-covered during this inspection. I met with EQT representative Zachary Subra upon arriving on Pad B. He showed me the location of the fluid discovered earlier in the day. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) present on the pad is in the northeast corner of the pad. The fluid on the pad surface is northeast of the MASS. The fluid in this area had an electrical conductivity (EC) of greater than 19.99 mS/cm. A thin layer of fluid covered approximately 20 square feet of the visible pad surface. The secondary containments for the heaters and pumps near this area of the pad had only snow and ice within them. The secondary containment at the southeast side of the MASS had fluid in it with EC of 700 to 1100 mS/cm. This containment appears to be in good condition and did not appear to be at risk of over-topping. Mr. Subra stated that there is also fluid with elevated EC at the northeast outlet of the north stormwater channel. The fluid was observed beginning at the east end of the rip rap at the end of the channel and extended for approximately 10-15ft farther to the northeast. This flow did not appear to reach the line of compost filter sock present approximately 5ft farther to the northeast. The fluid here ranged from 11.85 mS/cm to >19.99 mS/cm. The pad side slopes and the full length of the north stormwater channel was snow covered. The ground at the toe of the east pad side slope was also snow-covered and appeared frozen. Mr. Subra stated during the inspection that the suspected source of the fluid is the MASS since no other source could be identified. He stated that the space between the primary and secondary walls on the MASS contains fluid but the sensors on the MASS had not alerted them to elevated EC in this space. He also stated toward the end of this inspection that these sensors had been recalibrated and that they were now indicating that the fluid in this space has a high EC reading but he did not state what the reading was. I made the following recommendations to Mr. Subra during this inspection. The Department recommends not adding any additional fluid to the MASS. The Department recommends installing a sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel and collecting the fluid from this sump for the duration of the frac. The Department recommends emptying and disassembling the MASS. The Department recommends installing a trench, if possible, at the northeast corner of the pad to collect fluid before it makes its way into the north stormwater channel. The Department recommends monitoring this trench and the sump for electrical conductivity. I took sample 0718-197 from the east end of the north stormwater channel. I took sample 0718-198 from the northeast corner of the pad, next to the northeast side of the MASS. Both samples will be sent to the state laboratory. Sample 0718-197 will be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Al, Br, and Li. Sample 0718-198 will be analyzed for the 942 metals plus Al, Br, and Li. On 12/20/22 Rick Hall of EQT emailed the Department a report detailing the results of EQT's investigation of the release. The report states, in summary, that a combination of things led to the release including a hole in the secondary containment liner of the interstitial space between each wall of the MASS, an incorrectly installed electrical conductivity meter in this space which lead to inconsistent readings, and a check valve installed backwards which led to a truck driver successfully off-loading produced fluid into the interstitial space. The report also stated that EQT is committed to pursuing remediation of this release under Act 2.Violations noted.

A screw has been inserted into the brine tank to help stop the leak. Drips were observed coming out of the leak area. During the inspection I observed a dead spot of vegetation extending approximately 55' long and approximately 16' in the widest spot. The soil was inundated with deer tracks. I used a soil Hanna Groline soil probe to screen for conductivity. All readings exceeded the meters range of 4.00 mS/cm. Fluids still remain within the poly brine tank and the well is active. The Department recommends addressing the brine release. Violations remain outstanding.

Comments: The DEP (WQS Starkey) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Twin Ridge 02-185 well site located in Covington Township, Tioga County on 2/13/2020 at 0935 hours. Due to snowmelt and a small amount of precipitation, the collected stormwater within the southern basin had overflowed. Early readings of the overflowing water was field measured at 1496 us/cm and 13.07 pH. Repsol immediately began pumping the water within the basin into the frac tanks. Water overflowed from the basin last night for up to 5 hours but at a fairly low rate. Triple stack silt sock located downslope of the basin appears to have prevented a lot of the overflow from escaping the project area. No clear evidence of high pH stormwater escaped the project's permit boundaries. Repsol is working on in-house approvals for plans on the reclamation of the site to address the open violations against API # 117-21997. Violations against 117-21997 cited on 6/24/2019 remain OUTSTANDING at this time. No new violations were cited during this inspection. The DEP departed the site at 1105 hours.

Comments: Routine field inspection performed in late morning with cold, cloudy weather conditions, and 30 degrees. Last inspection performed on 7/26/18, more than 4 years ago. Wellhead is located in Agriculture field planted and harvested with soybean ~250' WSW of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead surface casing valve is closed, lower right side production tubular valve cracked open to port with closed valve to port and plumbed to drip/domestic house gas meter run, valve closed to stuffing box before meter and valve closed after meter to supply, production tubular left side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with no valve unions, and the production tubular plumbed on left side (opposite meter) of head to sales/surface equipment with closed valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photos #3 and #4). Meter reading and closed supply valve (photo #5). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility and does not require a well label/marker. Some trace to moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility and one 50 bbl poly tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #6). Valve closed on main tubular feeding facility and closed valves to and from separator (photo #7). No production chart recording apparatus present (photo #8). No Well posting signage is affixed anywhere at or near facility. Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment. Oil staining present at facility on ground near separator with in the containment (photos #6 and #7). Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add permanent well posting signage to be affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 0 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021, 2020, 2019, 2018, and 2017 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2015 of 25.55 Mcf recorded over 336 days. This well continues to not be in production with valves closed (shut-in) at the wellhead to sales/production and to plumbed meter run before and after meter. Additionally, the main valve to facility is closed and there is not production recording chart apparatus at facility. This well has not reported production in over five years. This is not an active, producing well. The well is abandoned. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well abandonment OGA3220(A).

Report Details

Violation Code: OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
Violation ID: 981348
Permit API: 085-24161
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: West Salem Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 1/10/2023
Comments: Routine field inspection performed in late morning with cold, cloudy weather conditions, and 30 degrees. Last inspection performed on 7/26/18, more than 4 years ago. Wellhead is located in Agriculture field planted and harvested with soybean ~250' WSW of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead surface casing valve is closed, lower right side production tubular valve cracked open to port with closed valve to port and plumbed to drip/domestic house gas meter run, valve closed to stuffing box before meter and valve closed after meter to supply, production tubular left side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with no valve unions, and the production tubular plumbed on left side (opposite meter) of head to sales/surface equipment with closed valve; annulus is buried, unable to determine if vented (photos #3 and #4). Meter reading and closed supply valve (photo #5). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility and does not require a well label/marker. Some trace to moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility and one 50 bbl poly tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #6). Valve closed on main tubular feeding facility and closed valves to and from separator (photo #7). No production chart recording apparatus present (photo #8). No Well posting signage is affixed anywhere at or near facility. Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment. Oil staining present at facility on ground near separator with in the containment (photos #6 and #7). Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add permanent well posting signage to be affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 0 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021, 2020, 2019, 2018, and 2017 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2015 of 25.55 Mcf recorded over 336 days. This well continues to not be in production with valves closed (shut-in) at the wellhead to sales/production and to plumbed meter run before and after meter. Additionally, the main valve to facility is closed and there is not production recording chart apparatus at facility. This well has not reported production in over five years. This is not an active, producing well. The well is abandoned. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well abandonment OGA3220(A).

Comments: On March 5, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4151444.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/26/2026
Comments: On 5/26/2026, the Department conducted an at the former location of the Holchin 2 well site in North Union Township, Fayette County. This inspection follows-up to IR 4181294, where no Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) was installed at the site entrance per the Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) control plan. In response, violations were issued for failure to failure to follow the E and S plan.An NOV Response to IR 4181294 was requested from the operator by 4/30/2026. However, no response of any kind to IR 4181294 has been received from the operator at the time of this inspection. The Department issued an Order to Diversified (#445705) on August 15, 2025. According to the Order, Diversified is to restore the Well Sites within nine (9) months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/08/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 1/08/2027 in accordance with current regulations.The following was observed during the inspection:A well plugging monument with the API number displayed was observed in the former location of the gas well (photos 19 and 20). No evidence of a spill to the surface, such as staining, was observed at the former well site location. No equipment related to well plugging and/or production was observed on site during this inspection. No evidence of nuisance mud tracking was observed from the site entrance onto Cutler Road (photo 1). The former access road and well site are temporarily stabilized and have established some vegetative growth since the time of IR 4181294, exhibiting approximately 40% vegetative growth coverage at the time of inspection. However, the third-party disturbances identified in IR 4181294 due livestock grazing continue to occur on site. The Department continues to recommend that the operator document any third-party disturbances occurring on site, and take reasonable efforts to stop them and prevent accelerated erosion from occurring on site. Temporary Erosion and sedimentation controls are installed downslope of the access road (photo 10). An access road cross-culvert is also protected by Compost Filter Sock (CFS). (photo 13) The site E and S/Restoration plans are available in a mailbox on site (photos 4-6). No evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation due to well plugging operations was observed on site during this inspection. However, some areas downslope of the former well site appear to lack the temporary E and S controls shown on the E and S plan drawing. Therefore, it appears that the operator continues to fail to follow the E and S control plan. Based on observations from this inspection, the violations issued in IR 4181294 shall remain outstanding. The Department recommends continued seeding and temporary stabilization on site until 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage is achieved. The violation issued in IR 4177612 for failure to post the API number on site shall be closed in IR 4205025.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a81(a)3 - CASING AND CEMENTING - GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to prevent pollution or diminution of fresh groundwater.
Violation ID: 934386
Permit API: 115-22174
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/19/2021
Comments: On site today in response to a water complaint in the area. This is a FUI (Follow Up Inspection) for the (4) wells on the pad that were inspected on 10/14/21. They are the Howell 2H, 4H, 6H and 8H. All were in production at time of inspection. Remedial work was completed on the 2H, 4H and 6H wells at the end of 2017 to address previous violations cited on the 6H well. - Met w/ lease operator Ben Whitaker to perform isolated gas screenings of the cemented annuli. - All (4) wells have the (20x13) and (13x9) annuli isolated and venting to atmosphere. The (20x13) annuli are plumbed to surface via 3/8" SS tubing, the (13x9) and (9x5) annuli are plumbed to surface w/ 2" pipe. The (9x5) annuli are venting to a shared poly tank w/ an LEL of 100% and CH4 of 5%. Gas was detected in the(20x13) cemented annulus of the 6H and the 8H. Flow checks were performed by lease operator using an ALICAT micro flow meter. No gas flow was detected at any of these wells (20x13) or (13x9) cemented annuli. - The (20x13) and (13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad were left open and venting to atmosphere upon completion of gas screenings and flow checks. - Individual prod. casing pressures listed below: - 2H: 631 psi., capillary string - 4H: 618 psi., capillary string - 6H: 658 psi., capillary string - 8H: 660 psi. ** Although gas was detected at the (20x13) cemented annuli of the 6H and the 8H wells, no flow was detected via Cabots O&G's ALICAT micro flow meter. This appears to remain indicative of commingling, residual gas within the vent lines and/ or annular spaces. On 9/3/2020 The Dept. requested that Cabot assess these conditions further and contact the Dept. with Cabots assessments. On 6/26/2021 Cabot O&G submitted a "Gas Migration Final Report" including a summary of previous remedial work performed on wells and an assessment of these residual gas detections. - No other violations or obvious concerns were noted.

Inspection Date: 2018-12-13
Comments: I performed an INCDT inspection upon notice of a release of produced water reported to the Department on the Abbott Pad. The weather at the time of inspection was overcast and about 31 degrees F. According to the spill notice, CID#338740, Steve Watson (Cabot Oil & Gas) notified DEP Answering Service who contacted Jonathan Ulanoski (NERO - ER). Jonathan notified Mike O'Donnell (Scranton Office - O&G) that on 12/12/18 Tetra (water transfer contractor) was disconnecting a section of the transfer line on the tank pad. While doing so, approximately 1-2 bbls of residual frac fluid from the line spilled off containment onto the tank pad surface. The spill was reported to the Department within the 2-hour reporting requirement at 5:50 pm. It was reported that at the time of the notification the spill area had been coned off, covered with plastic, and secured for the night. On 12/13/2018 remediation efforts were to be put into place. Resource Environmental will be overseeing all remediation activities. On 12/13/2018, I met with Abby Vogler and Christian Mondy from Resource Environmental. Prior to excavating the area impacted by the release, it was noted that the highest recorded conductivity at any of the screened sampling points was found to be 0.446 millisiemens. After excavation the highest reading in the affected area was 0.148 millisiemens . The excavation (Photo 4) was about 2-4 inches deep in an area about 25' x 25'. There were approximately 3-4 yards of pad material excavated into a rolloff container (Photo 5). I spoke with Herb Swiney, Contract Safety Consultant,on site as well, who stated the site was secured immediately after the release and a rolloff container was called for. The container was to arrive the following morning, 12/13/2018, and excavation started upon arrival. The site was reportedly covered overnight and due to the freezing conditions, the release stayed mostly surficial. By phone, I then spoke with Steve Watson, Cabot representative. He indicated that systematic random sampling for Act 2 would occur this afternoon, (December 13, 2018). The rolloff container would either go to Alliance or Keystone landfill. A report will be prepared detailing the sampling results. While onsite, I also performed a RTNC E&S inspection. The access road (Photo 7) and pad surfaces were solid and stable, as was the cut and fill slopes of the tank and well pads (Photos 6 and 8). The vegetation was visible through the snow and appeared to meet stabilization requirements. There were no erosional anomalies noted during the inspection. There are violations attached to this inspection.
